title: scopeSummary.byDim drops untagged cards: route the columns through columnsFor
body:
## Summary
lib/research/scope.ts::scopeSummary rolls byDim up over source.dimensions only, so a card tagged `untagged` is counted in no column, and researchView.ts shows only columns with total > 0.

## Description
dimensions.ts::columnsFor({derived, hasUntagged}) exists for exactly this and has zero callers since the Phase 6 cutover retired ResearchTriageBoard/MatrixCoverage (lib/notebook/dimensions.ts:121-155). scope.ts:131 maps `source.dimensions` directly - the anti-shape dimensions.ts names ('what left an untagged card renderable by nothing'). A reasoned notebook from the door (sourceOf(nb), no dimensions declared, tagsOf empty) deals every fact/mechanism/reversal as untagged.

## Flow
- parseNotebook(research-ok answer) -> sourceOf(nb) -> buildCards -> scopeSummary
- byDim totals sum to 1 of 8 cards (only the steel-man, counter-case)
- fix: byDim over columnsFor({ derived: source.dimensions, hasUntagged: cards.some(c => c.dimension === UNTAGGED_DIMENSION_ID) }), then app/(studio)/projects/[id]/_part/researchView.ts:141 shows the Untagged column

## Expected impact
The creator sees the cards no column files instead of 7 of 8 cards vanishing from the dimension rail. Could break: any test pinning byDim length on the fixture (fixture has 0 untagged, so 7 columns stay 7).

## Evaluation
Claim: user - every dealt card is in some column
Before: reasoned research-ok notebook: 1 of 8 cards in byDim columns; fixture 39 of 39
After: predicted 8 of 8 / 39 of 39
Method: probe - scratch script over the cassette (Before measured); After not built because lib/research/scope.ts is outside this round's paths
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: lib/research/scope.ts:131-135; lib/notebook/dimensions.ts:157 columnsFor (0 callers: grep columnsFor app lib packages -> only packages/ui window.core's unrelated columnsFor); app/(studio)/projects/[id]/_part/researchView.ts:141
instrument: a case in tests/golden-path/notebook-source.probe.spec.ts: sourceOf(parseNotebook(research-ok)) -> sum(byDim.total) === cards.length (red 1/8 today)

title: Fact.source is typed required, but the door never asks for it and accepted facts carry none
body:
## Summary
lib/notebook/types.ts declares `Fact.source: string` (required) while NOTEBOOK_SCHEMA has no `source` on facts and parseNotebook-accepted facts carry `sources[]` only.

## Description
Every notebook from the door violates its own type: the 5 facts of the research-ok answer have source === undefined. Readers that treat it as a string (counts.ts fixed in 3a059a81; FactRow-era readers, card.source in cards.ts:113, any `.source.split`) are typed safe and are not. The validator's WIDER list (shape.ts) records three more type-vs-schema divergences that ARE deliberate; this one is not recorded anywhere. Fix: `source?: string` and let tsc enumerate the readers.

## Flow
- make Fact.source optional
- npm run typecheck -> N errors = the readers that assume it
- fix each (prefer sources[].name), gate green

## Expected impact
A reader that assumes a source string is found by the compiler instead of by a reasoned notebook at runtime. Could break: fixture-only screens that print the string.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the type tells the truth about door-accepted notebooks
Before: 5 of 5 facts in a door-accepted notebook violate Fact.source: string
After: 0 type-lies; reader count = tsc error count (unmeasured)
Method: probe - measured on the research-ok cassette; the tsc reader count needs the edit, which touches consumers outside these paths
Result: better
Gate: contract
evidence: lib/notebook/types.ts Fact.source; tests/golden-path/notebook-source-population.probe.spec.ts needed `as unknown as Facts` to model a door-accepted fact (3a059a81)
instrument: tsc error count after `source?: string`; then 0 after the readers are fixed

title: NOTEBOOK-SCHEMA.md does not document unknowns[].probe, which the schema object and validator enforce
body:
## Summary
pipeline/NOTEBOOK-SCHEMA.md (the declared contract) has no `probe` field for unknowns; NOTEBOOK_SCHEMA, types.ts and shape.ts all carry it since c12015d2.

## Description
validate.ts calls NOTEBOOK-SCHEMA.md 'the contract' and every hand rule cites it. A terminal research run writes from the doc, so it can never author the machine form of an unknown's impact. The dialect now maps `probe` (71dcc3ee), but no run is told to write it. A derived instrument would catch the next drift: every NOTEBOOK_SCHEMA property's snake_case spelling (via dialect.ts's map, inverted) must appear in the doc's field tables.

## Flow
- grep -n probe pipeline/NOTEBOOK-SCHEMA.md -> 0 field rows
- add the field row in snake_case (when_mentions, forbid, require_one, no_causal_link, tests)
- probe: schema properties vs doc tables, 0 missing

## Expected impact
Terminal runs can author probes; schema/doc drift is gated. Could break nothing at runtime.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the contract document states every enforced field
Before: 1 schema property (unknowns[].probe, 5 sub-keys) absent from the doc
After: 0 absent
Method: simulation - doc grep taken; the doc is outside this round's paths (pipeline/)
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: grep -n 'probe' pipeline/NOTEBOOK-SCHEMA.md -> no field row; lib/notebook/schema-tail.ts unknowns.items.properties.probe
instrument: golden-path probe: invert dialect.ts maps, assert every snake key appears in NOTEBOOK-SCHEMA.md field tables

title: repairTurn has no production caller: a refused research answer is recorded, never repaired
body:
## Summary
lib/text/repair.ts::repairTurn (bounded repair of a refused notebook, consuming notebookFindings) is called only from tests; research.ts records NotebookRefused with its draft and stops.

## Description
failure.ts and validate.ts both justify `draft` and path-addressed findings by 'a repair turn can fix the listed paths instead of the run starting over'. grep repairTurn( in lib app packages workers -> only its definition. Wiring it into the research producer spends a second Claude turn per refusal (seat, not Gemini) and changes what a refused run produces - a product direction for the owner.

## Flow
- research turn -> parseNotebook refuses -> NotebookRefused(draft) -> turn failed bad-response
- no step calls repairTurn

## Expected impact
Owner decides whether refused runs self-repair. Could change run cost/latency.

## Evaluation
Claim: other - the documented repair path is unwired
Before: 0 production callers of repairTurn
After: n/a (direction)
Method: probe - caller grep
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: direction
evidence: grep -rn 'repairTurn' lib app packages workers --include=*.ts -> lib/text/repair.ts:193 only
